rules.name: USEM Serial Number Class Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the Qualys SERIAL_NUMBER, the one identifier that stays with a machine while names and addresses get reused, but only inside the CMDB class the scanned OS text points at, so a Red Hat host can land only on a Linux Server and a Windows Server carrying the same serial is never seen. It opens the chain because a unique serial inside the right class is the strongest evidence the feed offers.
rules.reads: SERIAL_NUMBER (sourceValue) plus sourcePayload.OS; the IP and DNS fields are not read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the single CI in the OS-implied class (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) whose serial_number equals the trimmed serial; null in every other case.

mechanics.title: Empty serial guard
mechanics.detail: If sourceValue is empty (null, undefined or an empty string) the script returns null at once; nothing else in the payload is read.

mechanics.title: Trim the serial
mechanics.detail: sourceValue is coerced to a string and trimmed; that trimmed value, with its case unchanged, is the value the search uses. Sample: 'VMware-42 1a 9c 3f 7d 2e 61 b8-55 04 e2 91 6a 27 c3 08' passes through untouched.

mechanics.title: Placeholder and length guard
mechanics.detail: A serial shorter than four characters is refused, and so is one whose lower-cased form, wrapped in commas, is found in the placeholder list quoted in full under literals, because such vendor values sit on dozens of CIs.

mechanics.title: Resolve the ignored classes
mechanics.detail: If the framework defined a non-empty _ignoreClass variable its string value is used; otherwise the script reads gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). An empty result means no class filter is added to the query.

mechanics.title: Class from the OS
mechanics.detail: classFor(sourcePayload.OS) casts the OS to a lower-cased string; more than two '/'-separated parts gives no class; else the first keyword hit in order (esx, windows, aix, solaris, hp-ux, netapp, printer, linux, cisco) names the class. No class: null.

mechanics.title: Open the class table
mechanics.detail: A GlideRecord is opened on the class chosen; its sub-classes come along by table inheritance. If gr.isValid() is false the class is not installed on the instance and the rule returns null.

mechanics.title: Query the serial inside the class
mechanics.detail: addQuery('serial_number', serial) as an exact match, plus addQuery('sys_class_name', 'NOT IN', ignore) when the ignore list is non-empty; then query() with no setLimit.

mechanics.title: Exactly one row
mechanics.detail: If next() is false the rule returns null. The first row's getUniqueValue() is held; if hasNext() is true a second CI in the class carries the same serial (cloned VM, serial typed on the wrong record) and the rule returns null; else the held sys_id is returned.

declines: sourceValue is empty
the trimmed serial is shorter than four characters
the lower-cased serial is one of the placeholder tokens in the junk list
sourcePayload.OS is empty or contains none of the classFor keywords
the OS text holds three or more '/'-separated guesses (split('/').length > 2)
the class table named by classFor is not valid on the instance (gr.isValid() false)
no CI in that class (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) carries the serial
two or more CIs in that class carry the serial (hasNext() true), whatever their state, class depth or address

rules.before: Nothing custom runs before it; it is the first rule of the chain, so every host that reports a serial reaches it (in this feed the Cloud Agent hosts; unauthenticated network scans rarely carry one).
rules.after: USEM Serial Number Hardware Match
rules.sibling_difference: Unlike USEM Serial Number Hardware Match it reads sourcePayload.OS, derives a class with classFor, searches only that class tree (the class and its sub-classes) and declines when the OS gives no class or the class table is not valid; the hardware rule never reads the OS and searches all of cmdb_ci_hardware. A second CI outside the chosen class tree that shares the serial is invisible here, so the in-class CI is still returned, while the same pair makes the hardware rule decline.

rules.name: USEM Serial Number Hardware Match
rules.purpose: Second and last serial rule: the same serial search, but across the whole hardware tree (cmdb_ci_hardware and every class beneath it: servers, computers, network gear, storage, printers). It exists for hosts whose OS gives no usable class (unauthenticated scans listing several guesses) and for CIs that sit in a different class than the OS suggests; its only safety is that the serial must belong to exactly one CI in the whole tree.
rules.reads: SERIAL_NUMBER (sourceValue) only; the OS, IP and DNS fields of the payload are never read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the single CI under cmdb_ci_hardware (any class beneath it, ignored classes excluded) whose serial_number equals the trimmed serial; null in every other case.

mechanics.detail: If sourceValue is empty (null, undefined or an empty string) the script returns null at once; nothing else in the payload is read.

mechanics.title: Trim the serial
mechanics.detail: sourceValue is coerced to a string and trimmed; that trimmed value, with its case unchanged, is the value the search uses. Sample: 'MXQ13005TC'.

mechanics.detail: A serial shorter than four characters is refused, and so is one whose lower-cased form, wrapped in commas, is found in the placeholder list quoted in full under literals, because such vendor values sit on dozens of CIs.

mechanics.detail: If the framework defined a non-empty _ignoreClass variable its string value is used; otherwise the script reads gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). An empty result means no class filter is added to the query.

mechanics.title: Query the serial across the hardware tree
mechanics.detail: A GlideRecord on cmdb_ci_hardware (no isValid check, no class restriction, the OS never consulted): addQuery('serial_number', serial) exact match, addQuery('sys_class_name', 'NOT IN', ignore) when the list is non-empty, then query(), no setLimit.

rules.before: USEM Serial Number Class Match already tried the serial inside the class the OS implies; hosts reach this rule because the OS gave no class (empty, no keyword, or three or more '/' guesses, as in the sample with seven), the class table was not valid, or the serial was absent or duplicated inside that class. Hosts with no serial or a placeholder serial were declined there and are declined here again by the same guards.
rules.after: USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC, then the name rules (USEM FQDN Class Match onwards); a serial that is not unique in the whole hardware tree is never used by any later rule.
rules.sibling_difference: Drops the OS reading, the classFor restriction and the isValid guard of USEM Serial Number Class Match: the search runs on cmdb_ci_hardware for every device class at once, so a serial shared by two CIs of different classes (which the class rule would never see together) makes this rule decline.

shared.helper: classFor(os) - input handling and multi-guess rule
shared.behaviour: Present only in USEM Serial Number Class Match, called on sourcePayload.OS. Returns '' for an empty OS. Coerces the OS to a string, lower-cases it and splits it on '/': more than two parts (three or more guesses) returns '' and the rule declines; a two-guess 'A / B' string still reaches the keyword checks. Checks run top to bottom with indexOf; the first hit wins; no hit returns ''.

shared.helper: classFor(os) - keyword to class mapping, first half (in check order)
shared.behaviour: 'esx' -> cmdb_ci_esx_server; 'windows' -> cmdb_ci_win_server when the text also contains 'server', otherwise cmdb_ci_computer; 'aix' -> cmdb_ci_aix_server; 'solaris' or 'sunos' -> cmdb_ci_solaris_server; 'hp-ux' -> cmdb_ci_hpux_server; 'netapp' or 'ontap' -> cmdb_ci_storage_server; 'printer', 'laserjet' or 'jetdirect' -> cmdb_ci_printer.

shared.helper: classFor(os) - keyword to class mapping, second half (in check order)
shared.behaviour: 'red hat', 'linux', 'centos', 'ubuntu', 'suse', 'debian', 'fedora', 'euleros', 'oracle enterprise' or 'amazon' -> cmdb_ci_linux_server; 'nx-os', 'catos' or 'cisco' -> cmdb_ci_netgear; anything else -> '' (no class, the class rule declines). The linux family is tested before the cisco family, so a text holding both words is a Linux Server; 'esx' is tested first of all.

shared.helper: Placeholder serial list (junk) and minimum length
shared.behaviour: Both rules: after trim, a serial shorter than four characters is refused, and so is one whose lower-cased form is a whole token of the comma-delimited list ',0,none,n/a,na,unknown,empty,not specified,not available,no serial,default string,to be filled by o.e.m.,system serial number,chassis serial number,0123456789,1234567890,' (the serial is wrapped in commas and tested with indexOf).

Both rules: sourceValue is coerced to a string ('' + sourceValue) and trimmed; the trimmed value is passed unchanged to addQuery('serial_number', serial). The script applies no case change, prefix or suffix stripping for the search itself; lower-casing happens only inside the placeholder test.

Both rules: if the framework variable _ignoreClass is defined and non-empty its string value is used, otherwise gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). When non-empty it is applied as addQuery('sys_class_name', 'NOT IN', ignore); an empty list adds no filter. The exclusion is by exact sys_class_name of each row, so sub-classes of a listed class are not excluded by the rule itself.

Both rules: query() with no setLimit; if next() is false the rule returns null; the first row's getUniqueValue() is held; if hasNext() is true a second CI carries the same serial and the rule returns null; otherwise the held sys_id is returned. No tie-break of any kind is applied: the second row may be retired, in another class, or on the scanned address and the rule still declines.

Only USEM Serial Number Class Match: after choosing the class from the OS it opens the GlideRecord and returns null when gr.isValid() is false (class not installed on the instance). USEM Serial Number Hardware Match opens cmdb_ci_hardware without this check.

shared.helper: agrees(), retired(), narrow(), isRealServer(), IP tie-break, loopback / link-local guard
shared.behaviour: None of these appear in either serial rule. Neither script reads the IP or DNS field, tests the scanned address, checks install_status, operational_status or life cycle stage, compares the CI class with the OS after the search, or treats twin records specially: any second row carrying the serial, live or retired, makes the rule decline.

rules.name: USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC
rules.purpose: Trusts the Cisco Unified CM device-name convention: the first DNS label is SEP followed by the phone's MAC address. It sits after the serial number rules (phones report no serial) and before the FQDN and hostname rules so a phone label is never tried as a server name; it searches only IP Phone CIs, so a MAC clash can never pull in a switch or a server.
rules.reads: DNS field as sourceValue (sample sep64f69dd5c9b0.voip.bankofamerica.com). No payload field is read: sourcePayload is received but never used. Also reads the framework variable _ignoreClass or, failing that, the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass.
rules.returns: The sys_id of exactly one cmdb_ci_ip_phone record (sub-classes included): the owner of a network adapter carrying the MAC, else the phone whose mac_address holds it, else the phone named with the device name upper-cased (SEP64F69DD5C9B0). null in every other case.

mechanics.title: Empty guard
mechanics.detail: Returns null at once when sourceValue (the DNS field) is empty. sourcePayload is never read: the rule works from the DNS name alone, so OS and IP play no part.

mechanics.title: Phone label test
mechanics.detail: String-coerces the DNS value (no trim), takes the first label before the first dot and lower-cases it. The label must match ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$ exactly: literal sep plus twelve hex characters; anything else (a server named sepulveda01) returns null.

mechanics.title: MAC rebuilt in four spellings
mechanics.detail: The twelve hex characters are cut into six two-character pairs joined with colons. Four candidates are built in this order: colon form upper case, colon form lower case, plain hex upper case, plain hex lower case (64:F6:9D:D5:C9:B0 to 64f69dd5c9b0).

mechanics.title: Ignore list
mechanics.detail: Reads the ignored classes from the framework variable _ignoreClass when defined and non-empty, otherwise from gs.getProperty sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass with an empty default. Applied to the second and third attempts only, not to the adapter attempt.

mechanics.title: Attempt 1: adapter owned by an IP phone
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_network_adapter where mac_address IN the four candidates and cmdb_ci is not empty. Each adapter's owner sys_id is tested with a GlideRecord get on cmdb_ci_ip_phone; distinct IP Phone owners are counted once each in a map.

mechanics.title: Attempt 1 decision
mechanics.detail: Exactly one distinct IP Phone owner returns that owner's sys_id. Zero owners, or two or more phones sharing the MAC on adapters, fall through to the next attempt. An adapter owned by a switch or server is skipped because the get on cmdb_ci_ip_phone fails.

mechanics.title: Attempt 2: MAC on the phone record
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_ip_phone (sub-classes included) where mac_address IN the four candidates, with sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when it is non-empty. next() then hasNext(): one row returns its sys_id; none or several rows fall through to the name attempt.

mechanics.title: Attempt 3: Unified CM device name
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_ip_phone where name equals the label upper-cased (SEP64F69DD5C9B0), sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when non-empty. No row returns null; next() then hasNext() true returns null; one row returns its sys_id. No setLimit anywhere.

declines: sourceValue (DNS) is empty.
The lower-cased first DNS label does not match ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$: not a Cisco Unified CM phone label; the host passes to the next rule untouched.
No IP Phone is found by adapter MAC, by the mac_address field or by the device name.
The name attempt finds two or more cmdb_ci_ip_phone records named with the device name (hasNext true).
Two phones share the MAC on adapters or on mac_address and the name attempt then finds none or several: a shared MAC never declines by itself.

literals.name: Phone label regex
literals.values: ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$ applied to ('' + sourceValue).split('.')[0].toLowerCase(); no trim; the lower-casing is what lets SEP64F69DD5C9B0 match, the regex itself holds lower-case hex only

literals.name: Pair loop
literals.values: for (i = 0; i < 12; i += 2) hex.substr(i, 2); pairs joined with ':'

literals.name: MAC candidate spellings
literals.values: [colon.toUpperCase(), colon, hex.toUpperCase(), hex] -> ["64:F6:9D:D5:C9:B0", "64:f6:9d:d5:c9:b0", "64F69DD5C9B0", "64f69dd5c9b0"]

literals.name: Ignore class source
literals.values: (typeof _ignoreClass != 'undefined' && _ignoreClass) ? '' + _ignoreClass : gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', '')

literals.name: Adapter query
literals.values: cmdb_ci_network_adapter: mac_address IN candidates.join(','); addNotNullQuery('cmdb_ci'); owner verified by new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_ip_phone').get(owner); no ignore filter

literals.name: Phone record query
literals.values: cmdb_ci_ip_phone: mac_address IN candidates.join(','); sys_class_name NOT IN ignore (when non-empty)

literals.name: Device name query
literals.values: cmdb_ci_ip_phone: name = label.toUpperCase() ("SEP64F69DD5C9B0"); sys_class_name NOT IN ignore (when non-empty)

literals.name: Sample payload
literals.values: ID 41277345, IP 30.144.62.108, TRACKING_METHOD IP, OS "Cisco IP Phone", DNS sep64f69dd5c9b0.voip.bankofamerica.com; outcome: IP Phone CI SEP64F69DD5C9B0 via adapter eth0 carrying 64:F6:9D:D5:C9:B0

rules.before: USEM Serial Number Class Match and USEM Serial Number Hardware Match run first; phones report no serial number to the scan, so both decline and every phone host reaches this rule.
rules.after: The FQDN and hostname rules, starting with USEM FQDN Class Match; a null hands the host on unchanged. Hosts whose label is not sep plus twelve hex characters pass straight through.
rules.sibling_difference: The only rule keyed on a MAC address rebuilt from the DNS label and the only one that searches cmdb_ci_network_adapter by mac_address (USEM Load Balancer Member Match and USEM IP Adapter Match read that table by ip_address); it restricts itself to cmdb_ci_ip_phone so a colliding MAC on a switch or server is never returned. Unlike USEM Device Name Match it reads neither OS nor IP, has no address tie-break, and tries three places in turn (adapter, mac_address, name) rather than one name search; unlike the class and hostname rules it derives no class from the OS.

rules.name: USEM Device Name Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the scanned host name for the two device classes outside the Hardware tree, IP Phone (extends cmdb_ci directly) and Imaging Hardware (scanners), which the hardware-wide name rules never see and which report no OS to an unauthenticated scan. It sits right after USEM Hostname Hardware Match so ordinary hosts are already resolved and only OS-less devices such as Avaya stations (avx plus the tail of the MAC) and scanners reach it.
rules.reads: DNS field as sourceValue (sample avxdd008a.cc.bofa.com); from sourcePayload the OS (guard only) and the IP (tie-break only). Also reads _ignoreClass or the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the one cmdb_ci_ip_phone or cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware record (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) whose name equals the host label; when several carry the name, the single one whose ip_address equals the scanned IP. null otherwise, and null when the OS names a server, desktop or other classed system.

mechanics.title: Empty guard and host label
mechanics.detail: Returns null when sourceValue (DNS) is empty. The value is string-coerced, trimmed and lower-cased; the host is the first label before the first dot (avxdd008a). An empty first label returns null. No suffix or domain is used in the search.

mechanics.title: Scanned address
mechanics.detail: Reads sourcePayload.IP as a string ('' + IP), or an empty string when the payload carries none. It is used only to break a tie between several records of one name and is never a search key.

mechanics.title: Ignore list
mechanics.detail: Reads the ignored classes from _ignoreClass when defined and non-empty, otherwise from gs.getProperty sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass with an empty default; applied as sys_class_name NOT IN on both class queries whenever the list is non-empty.

mechanics.title: OS guard through classFor
mechanics.detail: Lower-cases sourcePayload.OS (empty when absent) and calls classFor. Null when the class is non-empty, not cmdb_ci_linux_server and the whole OS text lacks the word phone. No OS, Unknown OS, a keyword-free vendor name or a Linux fingerprint passes.

mechanics.title: What the OS guard rules out
mechanics.detail: Every classFor class except empty and cmdb_ci_linux_server declines: ESX, Windows (server or computer), AIX, Solaris/SunOS, HP-UX, NetApp/ONTAP, printer/LaserJet/JetDirect, NX-OS/CatOS/Cisco. Cisco alone declines; Cisco IP Phone passes on phone.

mechanics.title: Search the two classes by name
mechanics.detail: Loops over ['cmdb_ci_ip_phone', 'cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware'], skipping a class whose isValid() is false. Each query: name equals host (platform equality, not case-sensitive), sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when non-empty; sub-classes included.

mechanics.title: Collect every row
mechanics.detail: Every matching row's sys_id is pushed to found; a row whose ip_address, string-coerced, equals the scanned IP is also pushed to onAddress (only when an IP was supplied). All rows are read: no next/hasNext short-circuit and no setLimit.

mechanics.title: Decision and address tie-break
mechanics.detail: found spans both classes. One entry is returned regardless of its ip_address. Two or more with exactly one in onAddress return that one. Otherwise null: none, or several with none or more than one on the scanned address. No retired or class agreement test.

declines: sourceValue (DNS) is empty, or its first label before the dot is empty.
classFor(OS) yields a class other than empty or cmdb_ci_linux_server and the lower-cased OS text does not contain the word phone.
No cmdb_ci_ip_phone or cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware record (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) is named with the host label.
Several records carry the name and none has ip_address equal to sourcePayload.IP, or the payload carries no IP.
Several records carry the name and two or more of them have ip_address equal to the scanned IP.

literals.name: Searched classes
literals.values: ['cmdb_ci_ip_phone', 'cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware'] (each skipped when new GlideRecord(class).isValid() is false)

literals.name: Host normalisation
literals.values: ('' + sourceValue).trim().toLowerCase().split('.')[0]

literals.name: OS normalisation
literals.values: os = ('' + (sourcePayload.OS || '')).toLowerCase(); pref = classFor(os)

literals.name: OS decline condition
literals.values: pref && pref != 'cmdb_ci_linux_server' && os.indexOf('phone') == -1 -> return null

literals.name: Phone keyword
literals.values: 'phone' tested with indexOf on the whole lower-cased OS text; its presence lifts the guard whatever class classFor gave

literals.name: Multi-guess threshold
literals.values: s.split('/').length > 2 -> '' (two or more '/' separators, three or more guesses)

literals.name: classFor keywords (substring tests, in this order)
literals.values: 'esx' -> cmdb_ci_esx_server; 'windows' -> cmdb_ci_win_server when 'server' is present else cmdb_ci_computer; 'aix' -> cmdb_ci_aix_server; 'solaris', 'sunos' -> cmdb_ci_solaris_server; 'hp-ux' -> cmdb_ci_hpux_server; 'netapp', 'ontap' -> cmdb_ci_storage_server; 'printer', 'laserjet', 'jetdirect' -> cmdb_ci_printer; 'red hat', 'linux', 'centos', 'ubuntu', 'suse', 'debian', 'fedora', 'euleros', 'oracle enterprise', 'amazon' -> cmdb_ci_linux_server; 'nx-os', 'catos', 'cisco' -> cmdb_ci_netgear; otherwise ''

literals.name: Name query
literals.values: addQuery('name', host); sys_class_name NOT IN ignore (when non-empty)

literals.name: Tie-break comparison
literals.values: ip && ('' + gr.getValue('ip_address')) == ip, with ip = sourcePayload.IP ? '' + sourcePayload.IP : ''

literals.name: Decision
literals.values: found.length == 1 -> found[0]; found.length > 1 && onAddress.length == 1 -> onAddress[0]; else null

literals.name: Ignore class source
literals.values: (typeof _ignoreClass != 'undefined' && _ignoreClass) ? '' + _ignoreClass : gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', '')

rules.before: USEM Hostname Hardware Match searched the Hardware tree for the plain host name and declined because IP Phone and Imaging Hardware sit outside that tree; every earlier rule needed an OS class, a serial number or a Cisco phone label (USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC), none of which an Avaya station or a scanner offers.
rules.after: USEM Management Interface Match, then the interface, service and address rules (USEM Network Interface Name Match, USEM FQDN Name Hardware Match, the load balancer rules and the IP rules).
rules.sibling_difference: The only rule that searches cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware, the only one that searches cmdb_ci_ip_phone by the plain host label (USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC searches it by the upper-cased sep label, by mac_address and through adapters), and the only phone rule that reads the OS and the IP. Its OS guard is inverted relative to the class rules (a class disqualifies instead of restricting the search) and it accepts a Linux fingerprint; it breaks a shared name by ip_address instead of declining outright. rules.name: USEM Hostname Domain Class Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the scanned DNS name split into a short hostname and a domain, and requires the CI's own fqdn or dns_domain to agree with that domain, searching only the CMDB class the scanned OS text implies so a namesake in another domain or class is never taken. It sits right after the exact-fqdn rules because it is the strictest name-based search that still tolerates a CI that never had the fqdn copied into its name.
rules.reads: DNS (sourceValue); payload OS (for the class) and payload IP (tie-break only); the framework variable _ignoreClass when supplied, otherwise the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass. The rule argument is not used.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the one CI of the OS-implied class (subclasses included) named with the short hostname whose fqdn or dns_domain agrees with the scanned domain, or the single agreeing CI carrying the scanned IP when several agree; null otherwise.

mechanics.title: Source guard and normalisation
mechanics.detail: Returns null when sourceValue (the DNS field) is empty. Otherwise coerces it to a string, trims it and lower-cases it; sample 'ah-1047132-001.sdi.corp.bankofamerica.com'.

mechanics.title: Split into short hostname and domain
mechanics.detail: Finds the first dot. When there is none or it is the first character the rule returns null (a bare label is left to the hostname rules). host is the text before the first dot ('ah-1047132-001'), domain everything after it ('sdi.corp.bankofamerica.com').

mechanics.title: Read the IP and the ignore list
mechanics.detail: ip is the payload IP as a string, or empty when absent. ignore is the framework variable _ignoreClass when defined and non-empty, otherwise the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass, a comma list of exact class names.

mechanics.title: Class from the scanned OS
mechanics.detail: classFor gives no class for an empty OS or three or more '/'-separated guesses; otherwise ordered keyword tests pick ESX, Windows Server or Computer, AIX, Solaris, HP-UX, Storage Server, Printer, Linux Server or Network Gear. No class returns null.

mechanics.title: Query the class table by short name
mechanics.detail: GlideRecord on the chosen class table (its subclasses included by the table hierarchy); an invalid table returns null. Query: name equals host (case-insensitive), and sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when that list is non-empty. No setLimit.

mechanics.title: Walk every row and test domain agreement
mechanics.detail: Each row's fqdn and dns_domain are read as lower-cased strings. A row agrees when fqdn equals the full scanned name, or dns_domain equals domain, or fqdn starts with host plus a dot and contains domain after position 0; agreeing rows are kept in good.

mechanics.title: Collect IP hits in the same pass
mechanics.detail: An agreeing row whose ip_address equals the payload IP exactly (plain string compare, no normalisation) is also added to ipHits; nothing is added when the payload carries no IP.

mechanics.title: Decide
mechanics.detail: Exactly one entry in good: return its sys_id. Two or more in good and exactly one in ipHits: return that one. Anything else (no agreeing CI, or a tie the IP cannot break) returns null. The count comes from the collected arrays, not from next then hasNext.

shared.helper: classFor(os) — guards and order (USEM Hostname Domain Class Match only)
shared.behaviour: Present only in USEM Hostname Domain Class Match; the Hardware rule has no classFor. An empty OS gives no class. The text is lower-cased and split on '/': more than two parts (two or more slashes, i.e. three or more guesses) gives no class. Otherwise substring tests run in a fixed order and the first hit wins; no hit gives no class. An empty result makes the rule return null.

'esx' -> cmdb_ci_esx_server; 'windows' -> cmdb_ci_win_server when the text also contains 'server', otherwise cmdb_ci_computer; 'aix' -> cmdb_ci_aix_server; 'solaris' or 'sunos' -> cmdb_ci_solaris_server; 'hp-ux' -> cmdb_ci_hpux_server; 'netapp' or 'ontap' -> cmdb_ci_storage_server; 'printer', 'laserjet' or 'jetdirect' -> cmdb_ci_printer.

'red hat', 'linux', 'centos', 'ubuntu', 'suse', 'debian', 'fedora', 'euleros', 'oracle enterprise' or 'amazon' -> cmdb_ci_linux_server; 'nx-os', 'catos' or 'cisco' -> cmdb_ci_netgear; anything else -> no class. Because 'esx' and 'windows' are tested first, 'Windows Server 2016 Standard' is a Windows Server and 'VMware ESXi 7.0.3' an ESX Server; 'Ubuntu/Linux' (one slash) is a Linux Server.

s.split('/').length > 2: an OS string with two or more '/' characters (three or more guesses, the fingerprint of an unauthenticated scan) is unusable and yields no class, so USEM Hostname Domain Class Match declines and leaves the host to USEM Hostname Domain Hardware Match. One '/' (two guesses, e.g. 'Ubuntu/Linux') is still classified by the keyword tests.

full = sourceValue coerced to string, trimmed, lower-cased. dot = position of the first '.'; dot < 1 (no dot, or a leading dot) returns null. host = text before the first dot; domain = everything after the first dot, so every remaining label is the domain. Nothing else is stripped: no suffix list, no marker keywords, no serial handling in either script.

ignore = the framework variable _ignoreClass when it is defined and truthy (coerced to string), otherwise gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). When non-empty it is applied as sys_class_name NOT IN ignore on the query, so it compares the exact class name of each row (no class hierarchy). When empty no class filter is applied.

GlideRecord on the table (invalid table -> null); addQuery name = host (case-insensitive); the ignore filter; query(); then a while/next() pass over every row, no setLimit and no hasNext. Rows passing the domain test go to good; those also carrying the scanned IP go to ipHits. Returns good[0] when good has one entry, ipHits[0] when good has several and ipHits exactly one, else null.

shared.helper: Domain agreement test (inline; there is no named agrees())
shared.behaviour: fqdn and dns_domain are read with getValue, coerced with '' + and lower-cased, so an empty field reads as the text 'null' and never equals a real name or domain. A row agrees when fqdn equals the whole scanned name, or dns_domain equals the scanned domain, or fqdn begins with host plus '.' and contains the domain after position 0 (its truthiness guard never fails: the coerced text is never empty).

ip = payload IP coerced to string, or '' when absent. During the row pass an agreeing row whose ip_address equals ip (string equality) is added to ipHits. The tie-break is consulted only when good holds two or more entries: exactly one ipHit returns it; zero or several ipHits, or no payload IP, decline. A single agreeing CI is returned without looking at the IP.

shared.helper: Helpers absent from these two scripts
shared.behaviour: agrees(), retired(), narrow(), isRealServer(), a placeholder serial list and a loopback/link-local guard do not appear in either script. Neither rule reads SERIAL_NUMBER, filters retired CIs, treats twin records specially, or re-checks the found CI's class beyond the table it queries; the class check is the search table itself, with subclasses included by the table hierarchy.

rules.name: USEM Layered DNS Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the scanned DNS name as it is kept in the discovery layered records (DNS Name -> IP Address -> Network Adapter -> CI) rather than in a name field on the CI record, so it finds hosts whose name is not written on the CI at all and resolves an alias to the real machine. It sits between the rules that read fqdn / hostname-plus-domain on the CI record itself and the plain hostname rules; the scanned OS is only a preference applied to the CI at the end of the chain, never a query filter.
rules.reads: Source field DNS (sourceValue); from sourcePayload only OS (class preference through classFor) and IP (tie-break between several CIs). No other payload field is read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the CI at ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci of the cmdb_ip_address_dns_name row(s) whose dns_name.name equals the normalised DNS value, when exactly one such CI passes the ignore list and agrees() with the OS class; when several CIs answer to the name, the single one whose chain runs through ip_address.ip_address equal to the scanned IP; null in every other case, and null whenever the CI chosen exists on cmdb_ci_lb.

mechanics.title: Normalise the DNS value and guard bare labels
mechanics.detail: Declines when sourceValue is empty or absent. Coerces the DNS field to a string, trims it and lower-cases it into fqdn. Declines when the result holds no '.', a bare label being left to the hostname rules. Nothing is stripped: the whole name is matched as is.

mechanics.title: Read the scanned IP for the tie-break only
mechanics.detail: ip is sourcePayload.IP coerced to a string, or an empty string when the payload has none. The address is never a filter on the query; it only decides between several CIs that answer to the same name later in the walk.

mechanics.title: Load the ignored class list
mechanics.detail: Uses _ignoreClass when the framework passes it non-empty, else gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). When non-empty it is applied as a NOT IN on the class of the CI at the end of the chain, so placeholder and technical CIs are never reached.

mechanics.title: Derive the preferred class from the OS
mechanics.detail: pref = classFor(sourcePayload.OS): the lower-cased OS text matched on keywords gives a class (Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server 7.9 gives cmdb_ci_linux_server). An unknown OS or three or more '/'-separated guesses give '' and then nothing is refused on class.

mechanics.title: Query the DNS Name to IP Address link table
mechanics.detail: Declines when cmdb_ip_address_dns_name is not a valid table. Else addQuery('dns_name.name', fqdn), addNotNullQuery('ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci') so the chain ends on a CI, and when ignore is non-empty ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci.sys_class_name NOT IN ignore; query().

mechanics.title: Walk every row and count distinct agreeing CIs
mechanics.detail: All rows are read, no setLimit or hasNext. owner is ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci; a row failing agrees() is skipped, not counted or marked. Distinct owners count once, first kept. With ip set, a row whose ip_address.ip_address equals ip marks its owner in ipOwners.

mechanics.title: One CI: return it unless it is a load balancer
mechanics.detail: When count is 1 the rule returns the first owner, but returns null when isLoadBalancer(first) finds that sys_id on cmdb_ci_lb: the name then belongs to a virtual address the balancer answers on, the host sits behind it and the load balancer rules take over.

mechanics.title: Several CIs: the scanned IP breaks the tie
mechanics.detail: When count is above 1, confirmed = Object.keys(ipOwners). Exactly one CI reached through the scanned address, and not on cmdb_ci_lb, is returned. None, two or more, or a load balancer as the one confirmed CI gives null; no fitness heuristic is applied.

mechanics.title: No CI: decline
mechanics.detail: count 0 (no DNS Name row for the name, no CI at the end of any chain, every CI on the ignore list, or every CI of a class the OS rules out) returns null and the host goes on to the next rule.

declines: sourceValue is empty or absent
the trimmed, lower-cased value holds no '.' (a bare label, left to the hostname rules)
cmdb_ip_address_dns_name is not a valid table on the instance
no cmdb_ip_address_dns_name row has dns_name.name equal to the value with a CI at ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci
every CI reached is of a class on sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass (or _ignoreClass) or fails agrees() against the class the OS implies
exactly one CI is reached but its sys_id exists on cmdb_ci_lb (load balancer device)
several CIs answer to the name and the payload has no IP, or none of their chains runs through ip_address.ip_address equal to the scanned IP
several CIs answer to the name and two or more of them are reached through the scanned IP
several CIs answer to the name and the single one reached through the scanned IP exists on cmdb_ci_lb

rules.sibling_difference: Unlike USEM FQDN Class Match, USEM FQDN Hardware Match, USEM Hostname Domain Class Match and USEM Hostname Domain Hardware Match, which query a CI table (the class the OS implies, or cmdb_ci_hardware) on fqdn or name, walk every row and break a tie by the ip_address field of the CI record, and unlike USEM Hostname Class Match and USEM Hostname Hardware Match, which query name and decide exactly-one by next() then hasNext() with no tie-break, this rule queries cmdb_ip_address_dns_name and dot-walks to the CI: the OS class is never the queried table but a preference applied by agrees() to the CI reached (shared among the name rules only with USEM Hostname Hardware Match); an OS that gives no class does not decline here as it does in the Class rules; the tie is broken by ip_address.ip_address on the IP Address record in the chain; an alias resolves to the real machine; and a load balancer device at the end of the chain is refused, which no other name rule does. mechanics.title: Decide exactly one

mechanics.title: Return the sys_id
mechanics.detail: Returns the kept sys_id. Class restriction plus uniqueness of the name inside the class are the only safeguards: the domain of the CI is never read here.

rules.name: USEM Management Interface Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the DNS label of a server management controller (HP iLO, Oracle ILOM, Dell iDRAC, IBM IMM, Cisco CIMC, generic BMC or IPMI), which is the server name plus a controller suffix, and returns the server CI named by the label without that suffix. It sits after the hostname rules because they have already shown that no CI carries the full controller label, and before the interface-name rule so that a '-mgmt' controller resolves to its server before any prefix walk on network devices.
rules.reads: Source field DNS (sourceValue). Payload field OS (sourcePayload.OS), lower-cased, empty when absent, used only for the controller marker words. IP and SERIAL_NUMBER are not read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the one record of cmdb_ci_hardware or any class beneath it (outside sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass and not a cmdb_ci_lb record or a class beneath cmdb_ci_lb) whose name equals the label with its last hyphen segment removed; null in every other case.

mechanics.title: Guard the input
mechanics.detail: Returns null when sourceValue is empty. Otherwise coerces it to a string, trims it and lower-cases it; the label is the text before the first dot, so the domain part never takes part in the match.

mechanics.title: Locate the last hyphen
mechanics.detail: dash is the position of the last hyphen in the label; the rule declines when dash is below 1, that is no hyphen at all or a hyphen in first position. Exactly one segment, the one after that hyphen, can ever be stripped.

mechanics.title: Read OS text and the ignore list
mechanics.detail: os is sourcePayload.OS coerced to a string (empty when absent) and lower-cased; sourcePayload itself is not guarded. ignore is _ignoreClass when the framework fills it, else gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). The IP field is never read.

mechanics.title: Controller evidence and the server name
mechanics.detail: tail is the segment after the last hyphen. If tail is in suffixes, base is the label up to that hyphen. Otherwise, if any markers entry is a substring of os, base is the same cut whatever the tail. Neither sign: base stays empty, null is returned.

mechanics.title: Search the whole hardware tree by name
mechanics.detail: One GlideRecord on cmdb_ci_hardware with addQuery('name', base) and, when ignore is non-empty, addQuery('sys_class_name', 'NOT IN', ignore). No setLimit, no active, status, address or OS condition; Hardware itself and every class beneath it are included.

mechanics.title: Decide exactly one
mechanics.detail: If next() is false the rule returns null. The first row's sys_id is taken with getUniqueValue(); if hasNext() is then true a second CI carries the server name and the rule returns null rather than choose. Retired records count like any other row.

mechanics.title: Refuse a load balancer
mechanics.detail: A GlideRecord on cmdb_ci_lb is opened; when the table is valid and get(match) finds the chosen sys_id there (cmdb_ci_lb or a class beneath it) the rule returns null. An invalid table skips the check. Otherwise the sys_id is returned as the match.

The last segment is not in suffixes and no markers word appears as a substring of the OS text
No cmdb_ci_hardware row outside the ignore classes is named like the stripped label
Two or more cmdb_ci_hardware rows carry the stripped name (hasNext() true after the first)
The single row found is a record of cmdb_ci_lb or a class beneath it (load balancer device)

rules.name: USEM IP Class Match

rules.before: USEM IP Adapter Match declined because the cmdb_ci_network_adapter records carry no ip_address for the host (newer discovery stores each address as its own IP Address record and may leave the adapter's field empty), or because its own owner-count, balancer, name or class checks failed.

rules.sibling_difference: Same distinct-owner logic as USEM IP Adapter Match, one link deeper: cmdb_ci_ip_address.ip_address -> nic -> cmdb_ci, with dot-walked queries (nic.cmdb_ci, nic.cmdb_ci.sys_class_name) and an isValid() guard because the IP Address table may not exist. It is the last of the four address rules.

shared.behaviour: Each rule is one function expression named process(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload), invoked immediately with those three variables; rule is never read. It returns a CI sys_id string or null; the first rule in the chain to return a sys_id wins and a null hands the host to the next rule. No setLimit, no orderBy, no try/catch and no gs.info, gs.warn or gs.error anywhere in the four scripts.

Identical in all four. ip = ('' + sourceValue).trim(); return null when sourceValue is falsy, when ip is empty, when ip.indexOf('127.') == 0 (loopback) or when ip.indexOf('169.254.') == 0 (link-local). Plain prefix tests on the string; no IPv6 form or private-range test is made.

Identical in all four. ignore = ('' + _ignoreClass) when the framework variable _ignoreClass is defined and truthy, else gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). Applied only when non-empty, as NOT IN on the exact class name: sys_class_name (Class and Hardware Match), cmdb_ci.sys_class_name (Adapter Match), nic.cmdb_ci.sys_class_name (Layered Match). No hierarchy on the list.

Identical in all four. Returns '' for an empty OS. s = ('' + os).toLowerCase(). If s.split('/').length > 2, i.e. the text holds three or more '/'-separated guesses from an unauthenticated scan, returns '' (no class); a two-guess string (one '/') is still classified. Keywords are then tested with indexOf on the whole lower-cased string in fixed order and the first hit wins.

shared.helper: classFor(os) - keyword mapping, second half (in test order)
shared.behaviour: 'red hat', 'linux', 'centos', 'ubuntu', 'suse', 'debian', 'fedora', 'euleros', 'oracle enterprise' or 'amazon' -> cmdb_ci_linux_server; 'nx-os', 'catos' or 'cisco' -> cmdb_ci_netgear; anything else -> ''. Because 'esx' and 'windows' are tested first and 'cisco' last, an OS naming both Cisco and Linux resolves to cmdb_ci_linux_server and 'VMware ESXi' never falls through to Linux.

shared.helper: How each rule uses the class
shared.behaviour: Class Match uses it as the search table (new GlideRecord(pref), sub-classes included) and declines when it is ''. Hardware Match keeps it as pref and applies agrees() to the single row found. Adapter Match and Layered Match keep it as pref and apply agrees() to each owner while walking rows, skipping owners of a contradicting class before counting. With pref '' nothing is ever refused on class.

In Hardware, Adapter and Layered Match. parentsOf reads sys_db_object by name and follows super_class.name upward: [table, parent, grandparent, ...]. agrees is true when pref is '' or cls == pref, when parentsOf(cls) contains pref (cls a sub-class of the OS class) or when parentsOf(pref) contains cls (cls a parent, e.g. cmdb_ci_server for an ESXi host). Any other class is refused.

In Hardware, Adapter and Layered Match; absent from Class Match. new GlideRecord('cmdb_ci_lb'); lb.isValid() && lb.get(id): cmdb_ci_lb and every class beneath it count; no refusal if cmdb_ci_lb is not a valid table. Applied to the single candidate only, never removed from the count: Hardware Match declines on server plus balancer; Adapter and Layered count a balancer only if agrees() accepts it.

Identical in all four. label = ('' + (sourcePayload.DNS || '')).trim().toLowerCase().split('.')[0]; empty label returns true. CI read from cmdb_ci by sys_id; name = ('' + ci.getValue('name')).trim().toLowerCase().split('.')[0]; empty name returns true. Else name == label, or label starts with name + '-', or name starts with label + '-' ('<name>-mgmt'). A CI named after another machine fails.

The DNS side is guarded by || '' and coerces to an empty label. The CI side is not: '' + ci.getValue('name') is the string 'null' for an empty name, so the empty-name pass fires only for a whitespace-only name, and an unnamed CI fails agreement unless the scanned label is 'null' or starts with 'null-'.

Class and Hardware Match: next() then hasNext() on the CI query, no setLimit, no ordering; two rows decline. Adapter and Layered Match: every row is walked and distinct owner sys_ids counted; count == 1 is required, so several adapters or address records of one CI count once. None of the four breaks a tie by scanned address, class depth or update time: a tie stays unmatched.

shared.helper: retired(), narrow(), isRealServer(), placeholder serial list
shared.behaviour: Not present in these four scripts. They read no install_status, operational_status or life cycle stage, so a retired CI is a candidate like any other and a second, retired CI on the address makes the rule decline. There is no twin narrowing, no walk from a load balancer service through pool and member to a real server, and no serial placeholder list, since the source field is the IP.
